[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Number of Unequal Triplets in Array** [LC 2475 · Number of Unequal Triplets in Array](https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-unequal-triplets-in-array/){difficulty="Easy"}

"All three different" is three conditions at once; its negation, "**some two are equal**", is about one value at a time. So count the complement: there are $\binom{n}{3}$ triplets in all, and a bad one has a value $v$ that occurs at least twice in it — either exactly twice (choose $2$ of the $c_v$ copies and $1$ of the other $n - c_v$ cells) or three times ($\binom{c_v}{3}$). The bad events for different $v$ are disjoint (a triplet cannot hold two different values twice each), so
$$\text{answer} = \binom{n}{3} - \sum_v \Bigl[\binom{c_v}{2}(n - c_v) + \binom{c_v}{3}\Bigr].$$
On the sample: $\binom{5}{3} = 10$, and the value $4$ ($c = 3$) spoils $3 \cdot 2 + 1 = 7$, leaving $3$. A direct count works too — walk the value groups in any order and charge each group as the **middle** of a triple, $\text{left} \cdot c \cdot \text{right}$ — and the two forms checking each other is the point of the exercise.

[Solved in full in @sec-cnt-pcomp-unequal.]{.card-link}
